en: The Philippine eagle is the national bird of the Philippines and is found only in the forests of Mindanao and nearby islands.
General Emilio Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain on June 12, 1898, at his home in Kawit, Cavite.
The Supreme Court of the Philippines, located in Manila, holds the judicial power to interpret the country's laws.
The Ifugao people built the Banaue Rice Terraces in the Cordillera mountains over two thousand years ago.
The sampaguita, a small white flower with a sweet fragrance, was declared the national flower of the Philippines in 1934.
Dr. Fe del Mundo created a bamboo incubator to provide affordable healthcare for newborn babies in rural Philippine areas.
Filipino and English are the two official languages of the Philippines, while Cebuano is the most widely spoken regional language.
The Sinulog Festival in Cebu City honors the Santo Niño with a vibrant street dance held every third Sunday of January.
Every Filipino citizen aged eighteen and older has the constitutional right and duty to vote in national and local elections.
National Artist Fernando Amorsolo is famous for his paintings depicting rural Philippine landscapes illuminated by bright, golden sunlight.
The Filipino value of bayanihan involves community members physically carrying a traditional nipa hut to help a family relocate.
Intramuros, the historic walled city in Manila, was built by the Spanish in the sixteenth century to serve as the government seat.
